USGS daily discharge, May 29, 1987 through December 25, 2022, on the $\log (1+x)$ scale with $x$ in m$^3$/s. Dashed lines are approximate current-rating discharge equivalents of current NWS minor and major stage categories at BTEC1/USGS 11160500, computed from USGS rating 40.0 \citep {cnrfc_btec1,usgs_11160500_rating40}. They give magnitude references rather than historical flood-stage classifications of daily means.\relax

Synthesized exAL-M-T1 prediction at December 25, 2022, on the $\log (1+x)$ scale, with $x$ in m$^3$/s. The 19 historical and 28 forecast dates show green historical observations and red open-circle verification values. The origin is $T$; the first lead is $T+1$. The maroon line is the predictive mean, the pink band is the pointwise central 95\% predictive interval (2.5th--97.5th percentiles), and ten gray traces connect predictive sample values within each period. Orange GloFAS and purple NWM products give source context; NWM denotes the NWS product family. Horizontal guides mark approximately 182 and 429~m$^3$/s. Figures~\ref {fig:forecast_origins_2021_early} and \ref {fig:forecast_origins_2021_2022} use the same conventions and vertical scale.\relax

The vertical line marks the origin $T$ and the first target is $T+1$.\relax

The labeled May inset displays the same predictions and source products over the range 0--1.3 to show low-flow variation.\relax
